extracted.intended_audience: predoctoral students applying for NIH F31 fellowships, their mentors, and institutional grants administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-level requirements for preparing and submitting a Predoctoral Individual National Research Service Award (F31) fellowship application to NIH, including eligibility, application components, and administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the F31 (Program intent)
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide predoctoral individuals with supervised research training in specified health and health-related areas leading toward the research degree (e.g., Ph.D.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Kirschstein-NRSA F31 program is intended to enable promising predoctoral students to obtain mentored research training while conducting dissertation research and to develop into productive, independent research scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible organizations include U.S. domestic institutions and Foreign Institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read the Eligibility section of each funding opportunity for opportunity-specific organization eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI citizenship and career-stage eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PI U.S. citizenship requirement: Yes. Career Stage: Predoctoral — U.S. citizen or permanent resident, enrolled in a research doctoral degree program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read the Eligibility section of the specific funding opportunity for any additional PD/PI eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding instrument and category
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding Instrument: Grant. Funding Category: Research Training and Career Development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The F31 is awarded as a grant under the training and career development category; applicants and institutions should plan budgets and scope accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget mechanism code
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Mechanism Code: TR - Training, Individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the TR mechanism code when preparing budget and administrative components for an F31 application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored training requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F31 awards provide mentored research training; applications should describe and document a mentorship plan and mentor commitment consistent with a mentored predoctoral fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must include the required number of reference letters as specified; follow the funding opportunity and Application Guide instructions for submission and formatting of reference letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Parent Announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent Announcements are available and can be used to submit investigator-initiated applications for a range of programs; they provide standard forms and instructions but are not topic-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all NIH institutes and centers participate on all parent announcements—check the participating organizations listed in the funding opportunity before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application instructions and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow guidance in the How to Apply – Application Guide, including any Fellowship (F) instruction call-outs, except where instructed otherwise in the specific funding opportunity or related notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must adhere to the Application Guide and any F-specific instructions; where a funding opportunity or notice overrides standard instructions, follow the opportunity-specific language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due dates and review/award cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Key Dates section of funding opportunities lists specific due dates; many opportunities indicate Standard Due Dates apply. Review cycles include Scientific Merit Review and Advisory Council Review, with noted earliest start dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the funding opportunity Key Dates for exact application deadlines and be aware of any policy changes (for example, changes to AIDS application due dates noted in NOT-OD-26-029).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating organizations and mission fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each funding opportunity specifies participating funding organizations; applications must fit within the mission of at least one participating organization and meet all opportunity-specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the list of participating institutes/centers for the specific opportunity (e.g., NICHD, NCI, NIMH, NINDS, etc.) and ensure the proposed research aligns with at least one participating organization's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH tools and resources to find opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Explore NIH Grant Opportunities tool to search Grants.gov and other NIH resources to identify active F31 funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage NIH tools (Explore NIH Grant Opportunities, Grants Process step-by-step guide) to find appropriate opportunities and understand application steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of contact and post-submission tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying, check the chosen funding opportunity for application submission, scientific/research, peer review, and financial/grants management contacts. After applying, find NIH staff assignments in the Status module of eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and use the correct NIH contacts for questions prior to submission; use eRA Commons Status to track staff assignments after submission. For technical issues, contact the OER Webmaster as directed.
